$comment: ASTRA rule catalogue, schema version dev

rules.statement: Every `astra.yaml` is UTF-8 and a well-formed YAML 1.2 stream of at most one document under the core schema, with no `%YAML` directive other than 1.2, no anchor or alias and no tag but the core schema's; in every document each string is a sequence of Unicode scalar values and each number is finite and within a double's range; and every record is RFC 8259 JSON text in UTF-8 with no byte order mark
Every key of a map is distinct: no two are equal YAML nodes, with the same tag and canonical form; and every name of a record's object is distinct once its escapes are read
Every map key is a string, and matches its key's type where the map has one (an `id`, or an `address` in `Universe.decisions`); every `id`-typed value matches the `id` grammar
Every address, reference, option reference and condition, other than a key of `Universe.decisions`, matches its grammar

Every required field is present: in `astra.yaml`, `spec_version`, `outputs`, `Output.type`, `Output.format`, `Input.path`, `Decision.options`, `Insight.claim`, `Insight.evidence`, `TextQuoteSelector.exact` and `FragmentSelector.value`; in a record, `spec_version`, `address`, `content_hash`, `size`, `generated_by`, `Generation.commit`, `Generation.environment`, `Generation.runner`, `Environment.iri`, `Runner.id`, `Runner.version`, `RecordedInput.entry`, `RecordedInput.content_hash` and `RecordedInput.size`
Every field is one the schema defines
`outputs`, `Decision.options` and `Insight.evidence` each have at least one entry, and no list of strings in an `astra.yaml` is empty
A declaration has exactly one of `path` and `url`
A declaration with a `url` has a `commit`
Every `commit` is a full commit id: 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits
Every declaration's and input's `path` starts with neither `/` nor `~` and holds no backslash and no ASCII control character, and an input's `path` also has no `..` segment and doesn't end in `/`
An option's `excluded` reason is not blank
Evidence has exactly one of `doi` and `artifact`, and has a `version` only with a `doi`
Every value has the JSON type its field takes: a string, a number, an integer, a list or a map
No list of strings holds the same entry twice (`Output.inputs`, `Output.decisions`, `when`, `requires`, `incompatible_with`, `insights`, `tags`)

Every value matches its pattern, enumeration or range: `Output.type` (one of `OutputType`), `Output.format`, `Evidence.doi`, `FragmentSelector.value` (a fragment identifier's characters), `FragmentSelector.conforms_to` (an IRI), `AnalysisDeclaration.url` (a remote URL), every hash, IRI and time, every `spec_version`, `size` ≥ 0, `Evidence.version` ≥ 1, `Resources.cpus` ≥ 0 and `Resources.gpus` ≥ 1
Every `astra.yaml` in the stack has a `spec_version` whose minor version the validator has the schema of

Every address resolves, through the declarations, to an element of the kind its field takes: an input or output in `Output.inputs`, a decision in `Output.decisions` and in `Universe.decisions` keys, a decision in conditions and option references, an output in `Evidence.artifact`
Every option named by a condition, option reference or selection is one of its decision's options
Every entry of `Option.insights` names a prior insight of the analysis

Every recipe placeholder is `{inputs}`, `{output}`, `{{`, `}}`, or an `{inputs.<entry>}` or `{decisions.<entry>}` whose `<entry>` is an entry of its output's `inputs` or `decisions` exactly as written
No two elements that one field could resolve to share an id (an input and an output, both of which `Output.inputs` takes)
No output shares its id with a declaration of the same analysis
A declaration's `path` stays inside the declaring analysis's repository
A declaration's `path` (at its `commit`, if it has one), or the top level of its `url`'s repository at its `commit`, holds an `astra.yaml` file, with no symlink on the way (§3)
A declaration with a `path` and a `commit`, in a file not read from a remote, names a commit the declaring analysis's repository has

A declaration with a `path` and a `commit` names an ancestor of the commit the declaration is in or, for a declaration read in the working tree, of HEAD or (during a merge) MERGE_HEAD of the repository that holds the declaring file
Every commit the stack gets from a remote, through a `url`, a file read from a remote or a gitlink crossed at a commit, can be fetched from that remote or was kept from an earlier fetch
An analysis from a commit, with everything it declares, is valid at that commit, `REMOTE_UNREACHABLE` aside
An input's `path` names a file (not a symlink, directory or gitlink), or something the validator recognises as standing in for one (§5)
An input's file, or what stands in for it (§5), is in the index of the repository that holds the input's analysis or, read at a commit, in that commit's tree there, reached through no gitlink
An input's file is inside its analysis's directory and outside every directory below it that holds an `astra.yaml` of its own
No input's `path` and no declaration's `path`, with `.`, `..` and repeated `/` resolved, is or lies in the `results/` or `.astra/` of an analysis of the stack
A universe's `derived_from` names a universe of the same analysis
No universe's chain of `derived_from` loops
Every universe's effective selection sets every active decision of its analysis and of every analysis reached through a declaration that a universe of its analysis drives
A universe itself sets only decisions whose `when` holds in its effective selection
Every effective selection satisfies the `requires` of every option it selects
Every effective selection satisfies the `incompatible_with` of every option it selects
No effective selection selects an excluded option
Every chain of declarations from an analysis's file is driven by all of the analysis's universes or by none, judged on their effective selections
No list of addresses, references, option references or conditions holds two spellings of one entry, and no universe's own `decisions` has two keys that spell one decision
Every spelling of one decision in a universe's effective selection selects the same option
Every output built per universe of another analysis read without a pin, and every decision of another analysis consumed, belongs to an analysis built in the universe being built

In the file of the analysis whose universe is being built, every address that reads another analysis's output built per universe without a pin, or consumes another analysis's decision, has its chain of declarations driven by the file's universes (a key in their effective selections goes through every declaration of the address, or the last declaration's analysis has no decisions and no universes of its own, the chain before it is driven, and that declaration leads back to no analysis already on the chain)
Every output read without a pin is active (its `when` holds) in the universe being built
Every pinned reference names an output

Every pin, read in the file it is written in, names a universe of the first analysis along its reference, starting from that file's own, whose universes drive the reference's declarations from that analysis's file to its last, or, where there is none, of the analysis whose output it is
Every pinned output is active in the universe it is pinned to
No output depends on itself, directly or through others
No reference to an output built once has a pin
Every evidence citing an output built per universe pins it
Every analysis with decisions, or with outputs built per universe, has universes, unless the root's universes drive it, or it consumes a decision
Every planned result has a record at `.astra/records/{universe}/{name}.json` (or `{name}.json` for an output built once), for each of its names, in the analysis it belongs to

The record at each planned result's place breaks no parse rule, states a `spec_version` whose minor version has a record schema or is greater than the checker's, and breaks no schema rule against that minor version's record schema, or against the open variant when that minor version is greater than the checker's
The record at each planned result's place has, as its `address`, the address that place is worked out from

The record at each planned result's place has exactly one `inputs` item for each entry its output lists at the commit the record names, matched by `entry`, and no other item (their order carries no meaning)

Since the commit in a result's record, nothing has changed in its output's declaration (command, inputs and their order, decisions, format), its decisions' options, the content of its inputs, never what stands in for it, or the results it reads
Every result's recorded bytes are at its default place
Every evidence citing a result cites an unchanged one
rules.status: the cited result's status; without a pin on an output built per universe, the worst of its results' (`missing`, then `stale`)

rules.statement: A runner writes a record for every result it makes, at the place of each of its names in the analysis the result belongs to, and writes the bytes to their default places

Every field of a record a runner writes is true of the run it records: the commit the recipe ran from, the hash and size of what it read and of what it made, the environment it ran in, the runner and its version, and the times
A runner records each recipe's environment as an IRI that it can recreate at its version

A runner runs each recipe in a checkout of a commit whose only changes are the records and results it writes itself, each result's bytes the recorded ones, and what a tool keeps of, or puts in place to drive, an analysis from a commit
A runner runs each recipe in the directory of the recipe's own analysis, in the checkout it runs in, even when another analysis drives it
A runner drives an analysis from a commit on exactly its files at that commit

A runner builds no result that belongs to an analysis from a commit, or to an analysis reached from it through declarations, and reads each of those results through its record at the commit that analysis is read at

A runner builds no output that reads a result belonging to an analysis from a commit, or to an analysis reached from it through declarations, while that result is `missing` or `stale`, or its bytes can't be got or aren't the recorded ones
A recipe reads the files inputs name, and other outputs' results, only through its output's inputs
